objective.statement: Convene a general-purpose council that selects its own roles, size and protocol from the task, explains every choice it makes, and lets the owner override any of them.
objective.charter: MANDATE. This is the default council for a task that does not match a specialised preset. Nothing here is fixed except the obligations: (1) SELECT - infer the roles, the seat count and the protocol sequence from the task itself, scaling seats up on disagreement, missing expertise, low confidence or deadlock rather than guessing a number up front; (2) EXPLAIN - every choice must come with its reason, so 'why is there a security seat and not a statistician' has a written answer before deliberation starts; (3) DEFER - the owner may override any selection, and an override is recorded rather than argued with. The stopping rule has two independent routes: either the council reaches a confident position with every objection addressed, or the owner approves after at least one round. The second route exists because a general-purpose council must be able to terminate on owner judgement rather than grinding toward a confidence number it will never reach on an under-determined question.
success_criteria: the role set, seat count and protocol are each justified in writing against the task
the owner can override any selection and the override is logged
seats scale on a declared trigger rather than an arbitrary initial guess
either confidence with objections addressed, or explicit owner approval, terminates the run

forbidden_actions: select a role set without explaining the selection
pick a seat count with no scaling trigger declared

sequence.custom_name: select roles, seat count and protocol from the task, and explain every choice

stopping.source_expression: (confidence >= 0.8 AND every_objection_addressed == true) OR (owner_approved == true AND rounds_elapsed >= 1)

conditional_decision_requires: the owner ratifies the auto-composed role set before the recommendation is acted on

metadata.title: General-purpose auto-composed council (the default when no specialised preset fits)
lineage: NOT DERIVED FROM 12-COUNCIL-PROTOCOLS-AND-PRESETS.md - no design entry exists
metadata.notes: SOURCE DESIGN: NONE - and that is the finding. This preset is REQUIRED by the spec (the schema's preset_name enum carries `general_purpose_auto_composed`, and the brief names 'a general-purpose AUTO-COMPOSED council that selects roles and protocol from the task, explains every choice, and allows owner override'), but a grep of all 72 preset designs in 12-COUNCIL-PROTOCOLS-AND-PRESETS.md for auto.composed / auto_composed / autocompose returns ZERO hits. No lane's doc-derived slice contains it, so without this file the required set could not be covered by any lane. It is authored here as an explicit GAP-CLOSER rather than assigned an ordinal in the 49-64 range, and the orchestrator should dedupe if a sibling lane also built one. || EDITABLE DIALS: everything in this preset is a dial by construction - that is what auto-composed means - but the ones an owner changes FIRST are: (1) participants.count.min/max (3..12) and count.elastic.scale_on, which decide how large the council may grow and what grows it; (2) participants.role_templates, the palette the selector may draw from - narrowing it is the strongest form of owner override; (3) protocol.sequence, the default stage order; (4) voting.method (`majority` is the declared DEFAULT, not a fixed policy - for a high-risk task an owner should raise it to supermajority or consent_no_objection); (5) stopping.expression's confidence threshold (0.8) and stopping.hard_caps (6 rounds / 90 minutes). || VOCABULARY MAP: there is no design row to map, so the mapping here is spec-to-schema. 'selects roles and protocol from the task' -> participants.selection.mode `automatic` with six strategies and NO pinned roster (a roster under automatic selection raises SEM-004 as a WARN, so the roster is deliberately absent and the palette is expressed through role_templates instead), plus count.mode `elastic`. 'explains every choice' -> participants.selection.explain_choices true, and the auto-compose protocol stage exists precisely to produce that written justification before deliberation starts. 'allows owner override' -> selection.owner_override_allowed true, deadlock.owner_intervention.may_override_vote true, and audit.safety.owner_approval_for naming role override. || WHY THE STOPPING RULE IS A DISJUNCTION AND NOT A CONJUNCTION: a general-purpose council meets under-determined questions where a confidence target may be unreachable in principle. One route stops on substance (confidence with every objection addressed); the other stops on authority (owner approval after at least one round, so the owner cannot rubber-stamp a council that never deliberated). A conjunction would let an under-determined question run to the hard cap every time. || NO WEIGHTED CLAUSE, DELIBERATELY: the schema also offers a `weighted` stop_expression, which looks ideal for an auto-composed council balancing several sufficient conditions. It is unusable in a documented preset - `unparse` emits WEIGHTED[...] >= t but the parser has no WEIGHTED production, so any weighted spec fails SEM-001 the moment it declares a source_expression and fails a parse(unparse(tree)) idempotence check. Confirmed with a control at platform/council/_probe_weighted_roundtrip.py. The disjunction above is the expressible equivalent. || NO CUSTOM METRICS: every clause uses a registry metric (confidence, every_objection_addressed, owner_approved, rounds_elapsed), so this is the one preset in the lane with ZERO SEM-012 warnings - a deliberate demonstration that the registry is sufficient for a general council and extensions are only needed for domain-specific gates.
